challenges.title: Hello, World — Your Dev Environment
challenges.description: Set up your local development environment. This is the foundation everything else builds on. A bad environment setup causes 90% of beginner frustration.
challenges.context: Before you write a single line of code that matters, your machine needs to be ready. Today is about getting your tools right so tomorrow you can focus entirely on building.
objectives: Install Node.js 20+ and verify with node --version
Install VS Code with essential extensions
Configure Git with your name and email
Create a GitHub account and SSH key pair
Push your first commit to a new repository

deliverables.label: GitHub repository with your setup notes
Terminal showing node, git, npm versions
LinkedIn post: Day 1 of your journey

resources.title: VS Code Setup for Web Dev 2025
SSH Keys for GitHub — Complete Guide

tips.text: Don't skip SSH setup — you'll thank yourself in week 2 when you're pushing code every day.
Install the Prettier extension in VS Code right now. Future you will be grateful.

challenges.title: Build a REST API with Express & MongoDB
challenges.description: Today you build a full REST API from scratch — routes, controllers, middleware, and a real database. This is the backbone of every web application you'll build from here.
challenges.context: You've spent 11 days learning how the web works. Today you put it all together. By end of day, you'll have a working API that a frontend can talk to. This is a major milestone — most students feel a real confidence shift after Day 12.
objectives: Initialize a Node.js project with Express 5
Connect to MongoDB Atlas using Mongoose
Build CRUD routes for a 'todos' resource
Test all endpoints with Thunder Client or Postman
Handle errors globally with an error middleware

deliverables.label: GitHub repository with clean, documented code
Specific commit showing today's API work
LinkedIn post about what you built today

tips.text: Don't hardcode your MongoDB URI. Use a .env file and dotenv from Day 1. This habit saves you from accidental credential leaks.
Write your error middleware last, after all routes. Express processes middleware in order.
Test each route as you build it — don't wait until the end. 4 working routes > 8 broken ones.

challenges.title: Authentication with JWT
challenges.description: Protect your API. Today you add signup, login, and route protection using JSON Web Tokens.
challenges.context: An API that anyone can access isn't production-ready. Today you learn the most widely-used auth pattern in Node.js.
objectives: Create user model with hashed passwords (bcrypt)
Build an auth middleware to protect routes
Test with invalid tokens and expired tokens

deliverables.label: LinkedIn post explaining JWT to beginners

tips.text: Store your JWT_SECRET in .env. Never hardcode it. Use a long random string — at least 32 characters.
